title: Resolved ALMA [C II] 158 μm Observations at Cosmic Noon: Interstellar Medium Structure and Dynamics of the Starbursting QSO SDSS J1000
question: Investigate the interstellar medium structure, photodissociation region properties, and dynamics of the starbursting quasar SDSS J1000 at Cosmic Noon (z = 1.8275) using spatially resolved ALMA Band 9 [C II] 158 μm and dust continuum observations.

recipe.goal: Reduce Herschel/PACS [O I] 63 μm spectroscopy and measure line flux
recipe.method: Reduce PACS nod cycles in HIPE, extract central spaxel spectrum with point-source correction, subtract continuum, fit Gaussian profile, and integrate flux over Δλ = 2 × FWHM
key_parameters: oversample=2 (spectral resolution 103 km s^-1); integration window Δλ = 2 × FWHM

recipe.goal: Measure ALMA [C II] line and 158 μm continuum fluxes, sizes, and spectra
recipe.method: Create moment-0 and moment-1 maps by stacking line channels, fit 2D Gaussians to cleaned images, integrate flux in circular apertures for main and satellite sources, and measure off-source aperture RMS scaled by sqrt(n_beams)
key_parameters: Circular aperture diameters: 1.45 arcsec (main [CII]), 0.35 arcsec (satellite [CII]), 1.05 arcsec (main continuum), 0.4 arcsec (satellite continuum)

recipe.goal: Model the far-IR to mm dust SED to derive L_FIR, SFR, and dust mass
recipe.method: Fit multi-wavelength continuum photometry (70 to 3038 μm) with a modified blackbody model using mercurius
key_parameters: Photometry from 70 μm to 3038 μm (Table 1); FIR integrated over 42.5–122.5 μm, TIR over 8–1000 μm
assumptions: Optically thin modified blackbody dust emission with κ_ν ∝ ν^β and CMB temperature correction at z = 1.8275; point-source photometry

recipe.goal: Fit 3D rotating disk kinematic model to ALMA visibilities and derive dynamical mass
recipe.method: Initialize spectral weights with initweights (dowtsp=True), fit continuum on line-free channels with UVModelFit, and fit 10-parameter rotating disk model to visibilities using UVModelDisk (KinMS + Galario + PyMultiNest)
key_parameters: dowtsp=True; fixed continuum parameters (RA offset 0, Dec offset 0, FWHM 0.22 arcsec, flux density 52.7 mJy); 10 varied disk parameters with priors in Table 2
assumptions: 2D Gaussian spatial brightness profile for disk and continuum; arctan asymptotic rotation curve; constant continuum in frequency; flat rotation curve M(r) = r V^2 / G for dynamical mass

recipe.goal: Model global and spatially resolved PDR conditions (n, G) and [C II]/FIR relation
recipe.method: Apply ionized gas and optical depth corrections to [C II] and [O I] luminosities, fit global line and FIR ratios with PDR Toolbox wk2020 models, and map spatially resolved [C II]/FIR and FUV field G across J1000
key_parameters: wk2020 model grid (A_V = 7, Z = 1); 1σ pixel masks at L_[CII] > 1.3 × 10^8 L_sun/px and L_FIR > 5 × 10^10 L_sun/px; fixed n = 10^4 cm^-3 for resolved G map
assumptions: [C II] luminosity multiplied by 3/4 (25% ionized gas contribution); [O I] 63 μm luminosity multiplied by 2 (optically thick spherical clouds); constant dust temperature across source; Kennicutt (1998) SFR-L_FIR relation

recipe.goal: Derive neutral gas cloud radius, mass, number of clouds, and filling factors
recipe.method: Combine PDR-derived density and FUV field with observed [C II] intensity and literature CO molecular gas mass in a spherical cloud toy model (Wolfire et al. 1990)
assumptions: Identical uniform-density spherical clouds illuminated externally by uniform FUV field G; n_H ~ n_H2; solar abundances
